facts.statement: Researchers argue that the holotype specimen lacked good autapomorphies, leading to the classification of the genus Rhamphocephalus as a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: They also argued that the specimen lacked good autapomorphies and the genus was a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: The genus Rhamphocephalus is classified within the suborder Thalattosuchia.
The genus Rhamphocephalus was named by Seeley in 1880.
Seeley noted in 1880 that the cranial bones of Rhamphocephalus were arranged more like those of a crocodyliform than a pterosaur.
facts.quote: Seeley (1880) señaló que los huesos del cráneo de Rhamphocephalus están dispuestos más como los de un crocodiliforme que como los de un pterosaurio.

facts.statement: The time range for Rhamphocephalus is estimated from 168.2 to 154.8 million years ago, spanning the Bathonian to Oxfordian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Oxfordian (168.2 to 154.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 10 recorded fossil occurrences of Rhamphocephalus in the Paleobiology Database.

Andres (2021) suggests resurrecting the genus name Dolicorhamphus for species formerly assigned to Rhamphocephalus, finding them to belong to a monophyletic pterosaur genus closely related to Klobiodon.
facts.quote: Andres (2021) resurrects the genus name Dolicorhamphus Seeley 1875 for depressirostris and bucklandii, finding both to belong to a monophyletic genus of pterosaurs closely related to Klobiodon.
